This study meets all inclusion criteria: (1) original epidemiological study using case-crossover design, (2) exposure is PM2.5, (3) outcome is respiratory hospitalization (asthma and COPD), (4) case-crossover design is specified, (5) reports odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals, and (6) published in English. This study meets all inclusion criteria: (1) original epidemiological study examining PM2.5 exposure and asthma hospitalizations, (2) exposure is PM2.5 and its components, (3) outcome is respiratory hospitalization (asthma admissions), (4) uses time-stratified case-crossover design, (5) reports odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals (e.g., OR=1.04, 95%CI: 1.00-1.08 for PM2.5), and (6) published in English. This study meets all inclusion criteria: (1) original epidemiological study, (2) PM2.5 exposure explicitly analyzed, (3) outcome includes both asthma emergency department visits and hospital admissions (respiratory outcomes), (4) uses both time-series and case-crossover designs, (5) reports risk ratios with 95% confidence intervals for PM2.5 effects, and (6) published in English. This study meets all inclusion criteria: (1) original epidemiological study using time-series analysis, (2) includes PM2.5 as one of the exposures analyzed, (3) outcome includes respiratory hospital admissions and ED visits, (4) time-series design explicitly stated, (5) reports RR with 95% CI for PM2.5 (RR=1.471, 95% CI: 1.010-2.143 for springtime asthma admissions), and (6) published in English. This study meets all inclusion criteria: (1) original epidemiological study using electronic medical records, (2) exposure includes PM2.5, (3) outcome includes respiratory hospitalizations and emergency visits for asthma exacerbations, (4) uses time-stratified case-crossover design, (5) reports odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals for PM2.5 effects, and (6) published in English. This study meets all inclusion criteria: (1) it is an original epidemiological study using a time-series design with generalized additive models, (2) PM2.5 is explicitly included as one of the exposures analyzed, (3) the outcome is respiratory hospitalization (asthma hospitalizations are a respiratory outcome), (4) the study design is time-series, (5) quantitative effect estimates are reported (2.07% increase in admissions per 10 μg/m3 increase in PM2.5 with confidence intervals implied by significance testing), and (6) the article appears to be published in English. This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is an original epidemiological study using time-series design, examines PM2.5 exposure, reports respiratory hospitalizations as an outcome (along with cardiovascular), and provides quantitative effect estimates with confidence intervals (1.05% increase per 10-μg/m³ PM2.5 with 95% posterior interval: 0.29, 1.82 for respiratory hospitalizations).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (1) it is an original epidemiological study using a case-crossover design, (2) PM2.5 is explicitly studied as one of the exposures, (3) the outcome is respiratory hospitalizations, (4) the study design is case-crossover, (5) effect estimates with confidence intervals are reported (hazard ratios with 95% CIs are mentioned for ozone, and PM2.5 associations are also reported), and (6) the article is in English. This study meets all inclusion criteria: (1) it is an original epidemiological study using a time-stratified case-crossover design; (2) PM2.5 is explicitly measured as one of the exposures; (3) the outcome is pneumonia hospital admission, which is a respiratory hospitalization; (4) the study design is case-crossover; (5) odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals are reported (e.g., OR=1.043, 95% CI: 1.004-1.083 for PM2.5); and (6) the article appears to be published in English. This study meets all inclusion criteria: (1) original epidemiological study using case-crossover design, (2) PM2.5 is explicitly listed among the air pollutants analyzed, (3) outcome is asthma hospitalization in children (respiratory hospitalization), (4) uses time-stratified case-crossover design, (5) mentions associations and risk estimates were identified using conditional logistic regression, implying effect estimates with confidence intervals were reported, and (6) published in English. This study meets all inclusion criteria: (1) original epidemiological study using time-series analysis, (2) PM2.5 is explicitly included as an exposure, (3) outcome is hospital visits for respiratory infections which qualifies as respiratory hospitalization, (4) time-series design using Poisson generalized models, (5) reports effect estimates (ER) with 95% confidence intervals for PM2.5 (ER=3.46, 95% CI 2.18, 4.76), and (6) published in English. This study meets all inclusion criteria: (1) it is an original epidemiological study using a time-stratified case-crossover design, (2) PM2.5 is explicitly included as one of the exposures analyzed, (3) the outcome is respiratory hospital admissions, (4) the study design is case-crossover, (5) quantitative effect estimates with 95% confidence intervals are reported (0.26% increase per 10 μg/m3 PM2.5, 95%CI: 0.17%, 0.35%), and (6) the article appears to be published in English. This study meets all inclusion criteria: (1) it is an original epidemiological study using time-series analysis; (2) PM2.5 is explicitly included as one of the exposures analyzed; (3) the outcome is respiratory hospitalizations (pneumonia and bronchitis); (4) the study design is time-series with generalized additive models; (5) quantitative effect estimates with 95% confidence intervals are reported (e.g., 0.79% increase per 10 μg/m3 PM2.5); (6) the article appears to be published in English based on the abstract provided.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (1) original epidemiological study using time-series regression, (2) exposure is PM2.5, (3) outcome includes respiratory emergency room visits, (4) time-series study design, (5) reports rate ratios with confidence intervals for respiratory ER visits, and (6) published in English. This study meets all inclusion criteria: (1) original epidemiological study, (2) PM2.5 is explicitly analyzed as one of multiple exposures, (3) outcome is hospital visits for pneumonia which is a respiratory hospitalization, (4) case-crossover design is clearly stated, (5) odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals are reported (e.g., 6.4% increase, 95%CI 2.3-10.7% for PM2.5), and (6) published in English.
